portInfo.description: Dammam’s cruise gateway sits inside King Abdulaziz commercial port on Saudi Arabia’s Arabian Gulf coast. An itinerary needs a controlled-port exit before it becomes a city day. The operator’s own city-centre estimate is 17.9 km/30 minutes, not “walk from the terminal.” Ground transportation and luggage handling are listed services; a daily shuttle schedule is not supplied. The destination is broader than a corniche photograph. Souq Al Hob offers a market-based introduction; Ithra in neighbouring Dhahran centres the day on art and culture. Al Ahsa’s caves and Hofuf market are separate inland ambitions requiring a long, line-validated excursion. They are not casually added to a short Dammam call.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Ithra Museum, 8386 Ring Road, Gharb Al Dhahran, Dhahran 34461: allow 2½ hours; check the actual gallery programme and accessible route with the venue.
Souq Al Hob/Love Market, Dammam: 75 minutes for market lanes and local retail. Meet at the operator’s specified market drop-off, not an unnamed city-centre point.
King Abdullah Park, Dammam Corniche: a 60-minute named waterfront stop instead of an undefined “corniche” address.
Murjan Island, Dammam: a separate 60-minute waterfront outlook, with transport arranged back to the same island drop-off. No boat operation is assumed.
Al-Qarah Caves, Al Ahsa: a 90-minute site block on a long escorted inland excursion only; verify cave paths/heat and admission.
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: Facility capability and sailing operation are separate. The operator’s undated “shuttle Yes” and “one berth” are useful logistics evidence, not a dated promise that tomorrow’s ship will call.
